summary: Accuracy drift and billing spike after mixed optimizer toggle — stepwise reversion guidance requested
description: Issue summary: BrightHealth reported an increase in per-request cost and a small but measurable NLU accuracy drift after an on-prem tenant-specific optimizer toggle deployed on 2026-03-10. The toggle enabled mixed-precision + aggressive KV prefetch for tenants on Dedicated pools. Impact: ~12% increase in token billing for the tenant's top route, 3–5% drop in exact-match on a customer regression prompt set, and increased 95th-percentile tail latency (from 320ms to 580ms) for sequences >512 tokens. Environment: Dedicated pool in us-east serving tenant brighthealth-prod; deployment applied via tenant optimizer profile v1.3. Steps to reproduce: 1) Send canonical regression prompt set (attached) to model redwood-neo-7b-v2 pinned to profile v1.3. 2) Observe and record per-token billing and EM metrics from console. 3) Compare latency distribution using span traces from the console. Observed behavior: billing spike appears within 10 minutes of a rolling optimizer toggle; accuracy degradation is small but consistent on the provided regression set and correlates with the switch to mixed-precision + prefetch. Hypothesis: aggressive KV prefetch is evicting critical prefix cache entries and interaction with quantized kernels is causing slight numerical divergence (quantization-induced rounding) that manifests as measurable EM drops on edge cases. Billing rise is likely due to increased token re-generation in client flows (retries) and longer GPU time due to fallback/inefficient kernel paths at certain sequence lengths. Temporary mitigations applied by customer: reverted the tenant's traffic to a shadow profile and rate-limited high-token routes. Supporting artifacts: console traces (link in comment), billing spike screenshot attached, regression prompt set attached.
investigation_notes: 2026-03-11 10:25 - Preliminary checks: SRE verified no node OOMs or GPU throttling in the dedicated pool. 2026-03-11 11:00 - Reproduced EM drop locally against the same model and profile under synthetic traffic; observed higher KV eviction counts during peak sequences. 2026-03-11 13:30 - Confirmed that fallback to fp32 kernels occurs intermittently for sequences >1024 when mixed-precision path encounters a misaligned tensor shape — increasing per-token latency. 2026-03-12 09:15 - Cross-checked billing records: top route showed 11.9% token cost increase month-over-month correlated with optimizer toggle time window.
temporary_mitigation: 1) Scoped traffic split: moved brighthealth-prod 100% back to stable profile v1.2 for latency-sensitive routes. 2) Applied per-route token limit of 2048 for the affected endpoint to prevent fallback kernel path. 3) Enabled extra telemetry for KV cache hits/evictions for the tenant. These reduced 95p latency to ~360ms and billing impact to ~+2% during mitigation window.
recommended_rollback_plan: High-level: perform a conservative, staged rollback that preserves safety for other tenants and allows for forensic capture. Step 1 (preflight): create a snapshot of optimizer profiles and deploy a tenant-scoped snapshot archive (snapshot id: bh-rollback-0326). Export last 2h of KV-cache telemetry and capture a full request archive for the regression prompts. Step 2 (quarantine): route new traffic for brighthealth-prod to a dedicated stable host pool (if available) or to a latency-priority lane to limit blast radius. Step 3 (stepwise revert): (a) disable KV prefetch flag only, monitor 30m for latency and EM; (b) if stable, disable mixed-precision and switch to fp32 kernels for the tenant; (c) if EM/latency/ billing metrics recover, promote changes to stable. Step 4 (validation): run regression harness (provided) against 1k synthetic and 200 real requests and verify EM and latencies within ±1% of baseline. Step 5 (post-restore telemetry): keep elevated KV and kernel traces for 48h. Rollback notes: avoid global toggles; perform tenant-scoped toggles. If any step increases error rates or latency, abort and escalate to Eng duty (on-call scheduler).
postmortem_actions: 1) Add a preflight optimizer compatibility test to CI that runs mixed-precision + kv-prefetch across sequence length ranges. 2) Implement a tenant-level circuit breaker that auto-reverts aggressive optimizer flags when EM or latency degrade beyond a threshold. 3) Update runbooks and add a ‘safe-revert’ API that atomically restores profile snapshot for a tenant. 4) Engineering to file follow-up PRs to make mixed-precision kernel fallbacks cheaper (github PR referenced).
